blocks.why: Normal night before an easy 10:00 report — start the month with a full tank.
Straight to bed after the BCN turn, because I report at 00:55 tonight and this afternoon block is the only sleep I'll get.
Home from the Dublin all-nighter and down as fast as I can — blackout blinds, phone off, up at 16:45 for the LHR report.
In the door at 02:35 off the London return; sleep now and let the four days off do the rest.
An hour in the afternoon to top up after two nights of broken sleep, without wrecking tonight.
Back on a normal night pattern on the first proper day off.
Keep the same hours every night off so the body clock stays where I want it.
Same again — banking sleep before the run of early starts.
Pull bedtime back to 21:15 local so the 06:10 report doesn't cost me a night — 45 minutes to get up and out.
Short nap after the Lisbon turn; keeps me human without killing the very early bedtime I need tonight.
Lights out at 20:00 local — tomorrow is a four-sector 12-hour day off a 05:40 report and I need the whole night in front of it.
Long sleep after a 12-hour four-sector day; a day off tomorrow means I can take the extra half hour.
Down at 19:25 local on the day off — a 04:35 report means the night has to start in the evening, not at bedtime.
Ninety minutes after the Frankfurt turn to clear the debt from a 02:55 wake-up.
Full night before the big one — tomorrow's duty runs to 06:51 the next morning.
Prophylactic nap before a duty that crosses the whole window of circadian low; finishes 45 minutes before I leave for the car.
Home at 07:46 after the Stockholm night; take what sleep the morning will give me and don't fight for more.
Second sleep the same day to get back on nights before the 08:00 sim.
Sim done, four days off — straight onto a clean night pattern.
Day off, normal hours.
Day off, normal hours.
Start easing bedtime earlier — the 05:05 report on the 18th is two nights away.
Down at 20:00 local. Getting to sleep this early is optimistic, but it's the only shot at a full night before a 17-hour day.
Home at 22:56 after a 17-hour day — bed almost immediately, and I can sleep in a little because report isn't until 14:40.
Two hours banked before a duty that lands at 04:13 tomorrow morning; out of bed 45 minutes before I leave.
In the door at 05:38 off the London night — sleep through the morning, accept it'll be a bit short.
Proper night on top of the morning sleep, ahead of a 14h35 duty that finishes after midnight.
Home at 03:50 off the Dublin return; get the main sleep in now while it's still dark.
Second sleep in the evening because tomorrow is a 04:35 report — this is the night, the earlier block was the recovery.
Longest sleep I can take after a 17-hour four-sector day; day off tomorrow so no alarm pressure.
Early night on the day off to cover the 05:40 report — up at 04:00, out at 04:45.
Short afternoon nap after the CDG turn, then three days off to reset properly.
First night of the block off — back to normal hours.
Day off, normal hours.
Day off, normal hours.
Full night before an afternoon report — nothing to fight here.
Home at 23:43, bed at 23:30-ish — tomorrow runs to 02:52 the following morning so this night has to count.
Lie down at 10:00 local even if sleep is patchy; the FCO sector home is at 02:00 body time and anything banked helps.

conflicts.statement: Rostered FDP is 16h11 (report 14:40 local, release 06:51 next morning), against a hard operator ceiling of 13 hours.
options: Query crewing before the day and ask for the MAD-ARN-MAD leg to be split off to another crew
Ask whether the duty is being planned with augmented crew or an extension you haven't been told about
If it stands, file the pre-duty nap at 11:30-13:00 local as a fatigue mitigation and log an ASR at the end

conflicts.statement: Rostered FDP is 16h56 (report 05:05 local, release 22:01), against a hard operator ceiling of 13 hours — and it starts before 06:00.
options: Push back on this one first; it is the worst duty in the month on paper
Ask for the ARN rotation to be dropped, leaving the FRA turn as a normal early
Confirm with the operator in writing what FDP limit they are applying to this pairing

conflicts.statement: Rostered FDP is 14h03, finishing at 04:43 local, against a hard operator ceiling of 13 hours.
options: Ask for the LHR night sector to be reassigned
Raise it together with the 18th, since the two duties back to back are the real problem

conflicts.statement: Rostered FDP is 14h35, finishing at 02:55 local, against a hard operator ceiling of 13 hours.
options: Ask for the DUB rotation to come off the back of the duty
Accept and protect the 8-hour night on the 20th-21st that this plan gives you

conflicts.statement: Rostered FDP is 17h02 (report 04:35 local, release 21:37) — the longest in the month, against a hard operator ceiling of 13 hours.
options: Query it as soon as the roster is published rather than on the day
Ask for either the ARN pair or the DUB pair to be removed
If it stands, the plan puts 7h30 in front of it and 8h30 behind it; there is no more sleep available inside the duty

conflicts.statement: Rostered FDP is 14h07, finishing at 03:22 on 1 October, against a hard operator ceiling of 13 hours.
options: Ask for the FCO night sector to be reassigned
Check what rest is rostered on 1 October before you accept it, since it falls outside this roster period

conflicts.statement: Release 14:54 local, next report 00:55 — 10h01 of rest. Two 55-minute commutes leave 8h11 of sleep opportunity. That clears the 8-hour requirement by 11 minutes and nothing else.
options: Any inbound delay on MD799 puts you below 8 hours; 117.25(f) makes that your call to raise, not the operator's
Ask crewing now for the 00:55 report to move right, or for a hotel at MAD to take the commute out of the equation
Decide in advance what your trigger is — e.g. if you are on blocks after 15:10 local you call it

conflicts.statement: Release 08:28 local, next report 18:30 — 10h02 of rest, 8h12 of sleep opportunity after commuting. Same 11-minute margin, and this one follows a full night duty.
options: Same trigger logic as the 1st: late off MD826 and the 8 hours is gone
Ask for the two duties on the 2nd to be split across crews
Consider a room near MAD for this one turnaround to buy back nearly two hours

conflicts.statement: Only 10h01 off at base between the BCN turn and the DUB night duty, against company policy of 12 hours at home.
options: Quote FCM §4.2.1 to crewing when you query the 00:55 report
Ask for the DUB duty to be pushed to the following night

conflicts.statement: Only 10h02 off at base between the DUB night duty and the LHR evening duty, against company policy of 12 hours at home.
options: Raise both short rests on the 1st and 2nd as a single query — it is one 36-hour sequence, not two separate issues

conflicts.statement: You get 8h11 between walking in the door and walking back out. Your own line is 9 hours.
options: By your own rule this is a night not worth going home for — take a hotel at MAD instead
Or move the line for this one turnaround knowing the 4 days off start on the 3rd

conflicts.statement: 8h12 at home between the Dublin night duty and the London evening duty — again under your 9-hour line.
options: Hotel at MAD for the daytime sleep, which also removes the two commutes from your sleep opportunity
Accept it as the price of the 4-day block that follows

conflicts.statement: Best available main sleep is 7h15, and it is scheduled 16:00-23:15 local — right through the evening wake-maintenance zone, so realistically you'll get less than that.
options: Accept the shortfall and lean on the 4 days off from the 3rd
Take the MAD hotel option and turn 7h15 into something closer to 8h

conflicts.statement: Main sleep is 7h00 in the morning after a full night duty — morning sleep is naturally short and the 18:30 report caps it anyway.
options: Set the alarm for 16:45 local and don't try to extend it
Add a 20-minute nap before you leave if you're awake early, keeping 45 minutes clear of departure

conflicts.statement: Main sleep after the 16h11 Stockholm duty is 6h30 in daylight — above the 6-hour floor but short of your target.
options: The second sleep the same evening (20:45-04:15Z) brings the 24-hour total to 14h, which more than covers it
Don't chase more in the morning; it will only push the sim-day night later

conflicts.statement: Post-duty morning sleep is 7h00 after landing at 04:13 local — daylight and a 05:38 arrival home limit it.
options: The 8-hour night on the 20th-21st covers the deficit before the next duty
Add a short afternoon nap on the 20th if you wake early, well clear of the evening

conflicts.statement: A 16h56 duty makes 7 hours of sleep in the surrounding 24 arithmetically impossible, whatever the plan says.
options: This resolves itself if the duty length is queried under op-max-duty-13h
Otherwise treat the 18th-19th as a two-day deficit and protect the 7h30 night on the 18th-19th absolutely

conflicts.statement: Same problem, worse: a 17h02 duty from a 04:35 report leaves no room for 7 hours in that 24.
options: Query the duty length first
Take the full 8h30 on the night of the 23rd rather than socialising into the evening — that is the recovery, and the 24th is a day off to allow it
